newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul to enter three countries in 1997.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul to enter three countries in 1997.

text.p: St. Paul Cos Inc said it plans to expand its existing international operations and enter three new countries in 1997.

St. Paul plans to enter France, Germany and Mexico in 1997 after entering the Netherlands, South Africa and Argentina in 1996, chief executive Douglas Leatherdale said in the company's 1996 annual report.
He said the company selected all of these international markets after careful analysis and said he believes they will become profitable sources of new business.

The company also said it will continue to develop regional strategies for emerging commercial markets in Europe, Latin America and Africa and said it expects additional growth in its international premium volume through its access to the worldwide markets served by Lloyd's of London.

Although the company said it expects its international underwriting operations to grow more rapidly in 1997, it said it does not anticipate any significant improvement in U.S. property-liability market conditions.
"Competition for business in the U.S. insurance market remains very tough," Leatherdale said in the report.
"In recent years the competition has focused on pricing. But it has gone beyond that. We're now seeing aggressive competition based on the terms and conditions of insurance policies," he said.
He said the company will emphasize strong underwriting standards and pricing discipline.
St. Paul also said it will strive to identify profitable new market niches, particularly in its commercial operations.
"Improving our Personal Insurance results will be a top priority, as will maintaining Medical Services' market leadership position," the company said.
St. Paul also said it expects to complete in 1997 the full integration of its Northbrook acquisition from Allstate Corp.
In addition to the international business, reinsurance also offers opportunities for profitable growth, he said.
"Reinsurers today face their most difficult operating environment in a decade with substantial price declines occuring in most major lines of reinsurance," Leatherdale said in the report.
"Large insurers -- who purchase reinsurance -- are buying less coverage and retaining more risk on their own," he said.
St. Paul Re's focus in 1997 will be to maintain profitability and competitiveness despite the difficult market conditions, Leatherdale said.
